main_body: A flat 4x3 tile ground patch of snow, drawn as a repeating pattern of grey-green mottling, pale blue-lavender blobs, white speckle dots and dark dashes. It is a ground surface with no standing volume.
top_band: none; a flat ground texture with no distinct top band or front face. A column read shows mottled grey-green with white dots and lavender patches.
evidence: The piece is a terrain ground tile, not a standing object, so it has no top and front structure to judge. It reads as a flat top-down ground texture, which is correct for ground. No side faces or fake volumes are drawn. For terrain kind, the 3/4 contract does not apply to a flat ground surface, so it is acceptable.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 5 tones: white, pale lavender, a light grey-green, a mid grey-green and a dark green-grey. There is no outline. The texture is a regular repeating motif: the same blob, dot cluster and dark dash recur at a fixed interval, so it reads as a tiled pattern rather than organic snow. The dark dashes and white dots look like noise and are not tied to any form. The lavender blobs are flat fills of about 5x5 pixels or more with no grain. The grey-green base is mottled but sits at low contrast and reads as murky rather than as snow. Next to the Beodeul grass and paving, which have clear value structure, tufts and per-stone shading, it looks busier but less crafted, with lower per-tile information in the large flat lavender areas. When in doubt, fail.
